title: Scary Movie 3
synopsis: There's a tape that kills you a week after you watch it. There are crop circles in your uncle's field. There is a rapper named George. Solve all three.

nodes.text: Your friend Brenda hands you the cursed tape. The cursed tape is, technically, a VHS. You haven't owned a VCR in years.

choices.consequence: “Find a VCR” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Plot.
“Refuse the tape” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Wise.

nodes.text: A pawn shop has a VCR. The pawn shop owner is also a rapper.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Plot.
You commit to “Take the rapper's number.” The story records the instinct as “Style” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You watch the tape. It is grainy. It is also, you realize, a karaoke video for a song you don't know.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Investigate.
“Just turn it off” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Wise.

nodes.text: Cindy, the protagonist of every Scary Movie, calls. She has been trying to call you for two films.

choices.consequence: “Pick up” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Plot.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Style.

nodes.text: Your uncle's cornfield has new crop circles. The circles, drawn by aliens, are also a math joke.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Solve the math.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Tourist.

nodes.text: Father Muldoon has, in his rectory, both an exorcism kit and a karaoke machine. They are, surprisingly, related.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Use the karaoke” back. Plot shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Use the kit.” The story records the instinct as “Plot” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: The aliens, polite, show up at the cornfield. They have a complaint. The complaint is, technically, valid.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Hear them out” back. Civil shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Generous.

nodes.text: The girl from the tape, Tabitha, climbs out of a TV. She is, off-camera, exhausted.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Civil—follows you into whatever comes next.
“Apologize” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Polite.

nodes.text: You end up in a rap battle. You don't know how. The rules are, somehow, clear.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Battle” back. Brave shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Forfeit.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Brenda has been killed by the tape. She is, however, alive in this scene. The continuity is, again, doing its best.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Style.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Comedy—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The President — also the protagonist of the parody — is, today, addressing the nation. He has, on his desk, a chicken.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Plot—follows you into whatever comes next.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Plot.

nodes.text: The press briefing involves, accidentally, the President saying the cursed tape song out loud. The press laughs. The aliens cry.

choices.consequence: “Stop the briefing” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Civic.
“Let it finish” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Comedy.

nodes.text: Cindy proposes a plan. The plan involves Tabitha and the karaoke machine and the rap battle.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Trust—follows you into whatever comes next.
You commit to “Modify the plan.” The story records the instinct as “Improve” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Tabitha's mother, somewhere, wants to be apologized to. Tabitha is, technically, the saddest character in the movie.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honor.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Direct.

nodes.text: The final showdown is a karaoke night at the local bar. The aliens are surprisingly good at backup.

choices.consequence: “Sing” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Brave.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The tape, finally, plays its full original recording. The recording is, in fact, a 1976 wedding video.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Plot.
You commit to “Just delete the file.” The story records the instinct as “Modern” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: The aliens, satisfied, leave. They take with them, oddly, the chicken.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Civil.
There is no taking “Run for the cornfield” back. Comedy shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Sue ends the movie with a freestyle rap about closure, family, and cursed VHS tapes.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Drop the mic.” The story records the instinct as “Style” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Style.

nodes.text: Credits roll. Bloopers. A cameo by an alien who clearly didn't sign the release.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Loyal.
There is no taking “Leave the theater” back. Practical shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Tabitha's mother, played by a famous comedian, hugs you. The hug, on screen, is the best joke of the movie.

choices.consequence: “Hug back” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Civil.
You commit to “Just smile.” The story records the instinct as “Style” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: A title card promises Scary Movie 4. Everyone, including the chicken, is back next year.

choices.consequence: “Plan to attend” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Loyal.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You become the karaoke champion of the county. The cursed tape, in fact, is the song that keeps winning.
The aliens decide to move in with you. They are, in fact, polite tenants. They pay rent in interstellar shrimp.
You attend the actual 1976 wedding via a time-travel sequence you can't quite explain. You realize the cursed tape was, all along, family content.
